method.universe: Women age 15-49, the DHS interview universe. NOT the same population as UNESCO's adult 15+ literacy rate, and the post must never present them as one measure.
method.values: DHS's own published weighted percentages, read from its public API. Nothing here is recomputed from microdata.

assertions.columns_sum_to_100: checked on all 226 surveys, tolerance 0.35 pts
assertions.sch_equals_literate_minus_whole_minus_pa: checked on all surveys, tolerance 0.15 pts

composition.rule: Latest survey per country among those using the current coding rule.
composition.medians_note: Five independent column medians across the same set of countries, NOT the profile of any one country. They do not sum to 100 and the first three do not sum to the median published rate.

no_card_in_language.note: Counted as NOT literate. A respondent who reads fluently in a language the interviewer had no card for is recorded as illiterate, so the instrument errs in both directions.

rule_change_all_countries.note: Every country with at least one survey under each rule. The four the essay walks through are worked examples chosen for readability, not the evidence base, and the essay must not imply otherwise.

rule_change.dhs_note: In DHS-VI and earlier surveys the question on the ability of the respondent to read a sentence was not asked to women and men with secondary education or higher than secondary. Thus estimates from earlier surveys may overestimate literacy relative to DHS-7 and DHS-8 surveys. Care should be taken in interpreting trends.
rule_change.dhs_note_source: The DHS Program, Guide to DHS Statistics, Literacy, Changes over Time

regimes_overlap_in_time.why_it_matters: The two regimes overlap, so a fieldwork-year cutoff misclassifies surveys. The classifier compares the never-tested column against both published education shares instead.

how_measured.source: UNESCO Institute for Statistics, via Our World in Data

who_is_tested.note: Membership is 'ever administered a literacy test in any year UNESCO records', which is the most generous possible reading. It is not a claim about the country's current practice.

method_vs_level.note: Each country's most recently recorded reporting method against the UNESCO adult literacy rate nearest that year.
method_vs_level.caution: This has two readings and the data cannot separate them: testing may be applied where literacy is already doubted (selection), and testing may produce lower numbers than self-declaration (instrument). The post must state both rather than assert the second.

tested_where_doubted.note: The tidy version of this pattern does not hold and the post must not assert it.

two_instruments.note: DHS and UNESCO adult literacy for the same country-year. Different universes and different instruments, so this is a disagreement between measures, not an error in either.
